house:/debates/2026/11/23/Oral Questions.summary: Minister of Jobs and Families says the process has started to pay every new Red Seal holder the $5,000 completion bonus, with a formal announcement alongside Canada's Building Trades Unions on Nov 24.
house:/debates/2026/11/23/Oral Questions.short: $5,000 Red Seal completion bonus rollout begins; announcement with Building Trades Unions Nov 24.

house:/debates/2026/11/20/Oral Questions.summary: Exchange over keeping a strategically important Canadian large-language-model company in Canada, and Patrick Pichette's role with the government.

house:/debates/2026/11/19/Statements by.summary: Conservative MP and tradesperson says the budget adds $5.5B to Team Canada Strong toward 100,000 new Red Seal workers by 2031, but gives no update on progress.

house:/debates/2026/11/18/Government Ord.summary: Budget 2026 debate: the government cites $6 billion for Team Canada Strong to recruit, train and hire skilled trades workers, and says the $5,000 Red Seal completion bonus is already available.
house:/debates/2026/11/18/Government Ord.short: Budget 2026 debate puts Team Canada Strong at $6B for skilled trades recruitment and training.

house:/debates/2026/11/5/Government Orde.summary: During debate on the health data bill, the government points to its newly published national AI strategy, 'AI for All', which names health and life sciences as a priority sector.
house:/debates/2026/11/5/Government Orde.short: New national AI strategy 'AI for All' cited; health and life sciences a priority sector.

house:/debates/2026/11/5/Oral QuestionsA.summary: Opposition presses the government on the environmental, community and grid costs of AI data centres.

house:/debates/2026/11/5/Oral QuestionsP.summary: Opposition presses on conflict-of-interest screens, noting the AI minister added Dan Goldberg to his ethics screen.

house:/debates/2026/11/4/Routine Proceed.summary: Petition from Vancouver residents asks the government to stop incentives, subsidies and fast-tracking for AI data centres, citing water, energy and secrecy concerns.

house:/debates/2026/11/4/Oral QuestionsA.summary: AI Minister Evan Solomon says the government will build 'safe Canadian AI' and keep jobs and intellectual property in Canada.

house:/debates/2026/11/3/Adjournment Pro.summary: Government says it has committed $50 million to expand the Canadian AI Safety Institute and is working with police and security experts on AI-enabled scams and election interference.
house:/debates/2026/11/3/Adjournment Pro.short: Government cites $50M to expand the Canadian AI Safety Institute.

house:/debates/2026/10/30/Oral Questions.summary: Bloc Québécois cites Radio-Canada reporting on internal documents suggesting Ottawa favours Alberta for AI data centres so they can be powered by natural gas.
house:/debates/2026/10/30/Oral Questions.short: Bloc alleges Ottawa steering AI data centres to Alberta to be gas-powered.

house:/debates/2026/10/28/Government Ord.summary: Second-reading debate on C-34 links it to C-36 (privacy and deepfakes), C-16 (non-consensual AI deepfakes) and C-25 (elections) as the government's online harms package.

house:/debates/2026/10/27/Orders of the.summary: Concurrence debate turns to whether Ottawa should fund the Red Seal program, with the government arguing Red Seal mobility benefits workers in every province.

house:/debates/2026/10/22/Oral Questions.summary: Secretary of State for Labour promotes the Union Training and Innovation Program as a path for young Canadians into the trades.

house:/debates/2026/10/20/Routine Procee.summary: Government MPs press Conservatives over voting against the Red Seal enhancement meant to train 80,000 to 100,000 young people.

house:/debates/2026/10/9/Oral QuestionsA.summary: AI Minister Evan Solomon describes the new national AI strategy as built on trust, opportunity and sovereignty.

house:/debates/2026/10/9/Oral QuestionsE.summary: Government says paid apprenticeship placements under Team Canada Strong open in early 2027, as part of a target of up to 100,000 new Red Seal trades workers.
house:/debates/2026/10/9/Oral QuestionsE.short: Paid apprenticeship placements under Team Canada Strong to open early 2027.

notice:/committees/status-of-women/45-1/.summary: FEWO's AI study continues with CUPE-Québec among witnesses.

notice:/committees/ethics/45-1/60/.summary: Privacy Commissioner Philippe Dufresne is scheduled to appear on ETHI's study of AI in algorithmic pricing.

notice:/committees/official-languages/45.summary: The Official Languages committee holds hearings on AI's effects on official languages.

cttee:/committees/human-resources/45-1/5.summary: HUMA held clause-by-clause on Bill C-266 (national framework on skilled trades and labour mobility), with ESDC's ADM for Skilled Trades answering questions. Next step is the report back to the House.
cttee:/committees/human-resources/45-1/5.short: HUMA completes clause-by-clause on C-266, the skilled trades and labour mobility framework bill.

notice:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/47.summary: PROC's AI and democratic institutions study continues with The Economist's acting economics editor among witnesses.

cttee:/committees/ethics/45-1/57/.summary: ETHI hears on algorithmic or 'surveillance' pricing, with witnesses saying firms can already set individual prices and wages.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/46/.summary: The Chief Electoral Officer appears before PROC on AI and elections, including how agencies disclose their AI use.
cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/46/.short: Chief Electoral Officer testifies on AI and elections at PROC.

notice:/committees/industry-and-technolo.summary: INDU is drafting its report on the opportunities, risks and regulation of AI in Canada's strategic industries.
notice:/committees/industry-and-technolo.short: INDU drafting report on regulating AI in strategic industries.

cttee:/committees/government-operations/.summary: At OGGO, the Ironworkers argue that 'buy Canadian' procurement must also mean 'train Canadian', citing union training centres funded partly through UTIP.

cttee:/committees/status-of-women/45-1/5.summary: Witnesses tell FEWO that AI protections are urgent and call for a right to opt out of chatbots and automated profiling for public services.

notice:/committees/science-and-research/.summary: The Science and Research committee is drafting its report on artificial intelligence.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/45/.summary: The Inter-Parliamentary Union's Centre for Innovation in Parliament briefs PROC on what makes a parliament 'AI-ready'.

cttee:/committees/status-of-women/45-1/5.summary: FEWO hears on AI and gender-based violence and on teaching ethical AI use.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/44/.summary: PROC examines labelling of AI-generated content in political communication.

cttee:/committees/bill-c-39/45-1/5/.summary: Canada's Building Trades Unions tell the Bill C-39 committee that visibility into upcoming major projects is needed to plan apprenticeships and worker training.

cttee:/committees/veterans-affairs/45-1/.summary: At the Veterans Affairs committee, witnesses including the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency call for military trades qualifications to count toward Red Seal certification.

cttee:/committees/international-human-ri.summary: The International Human Rights subcommittee studies AI's global effects on human rights movements, including a distinction between today's AI and superintelligent AI.

cttee:/committees/status-of-women/45-1/5.summary: FEWO begins its study of AI's impact on women, girls and 2SLGBTQIA+ people, focusing on deepfakes.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/43/.summary: PROC hears about AI-generated submissions to committees and MPs' growing use of AI.

cttee:/committees/human-resources/45-1/5.summary: IBEW and the National Electrical Trade Council testify on C-266, describing apprentices losing level standing when they move between provinces.

notice:/committees/ethics/45-1/53/.summary: ETHI is drafting its report on the challenges posed by AI and its regulation, considered in camera across several meetings.
notice:/committees/ethics/45-1/53/.short: ETHI drafting report on AI regulation.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/42/.summary: The Clerk of the House tells PROC about the House administration's AI working group and its long-term AI strategy.

cttee:/committees/human-resources/45-1/4.summary: ESDC officials testify on C-266; the Canadian Council of Directors of Apprenticeship is described as already working on interprovincial mobility.

cttee:/committees/house-affairs/45-1/41/.summary: PROC begins its study of AI and Canada's democratic institutions; witnesses warn about advanced AI risks, including superintelligence.

cttee:/committees/human-resources/45-1/4.summary: HUMA hearings on C-266 continue with the Association de la construction du Québec and others; witnesses stress retention of mid-career journeypersons needed to supervise apprentices.
HUMA starts hearings on Bill C-266. Canada's Building Trades Unions (Sean Strickland) back the Red Seal system and call for better coordination between governments and trainers.

bill:C-34:PassedHouseSecondReadingDateTi.summary: Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act, passes second reading and goes to committee. It would bring designated AI chatbot services under the same duty-of-care framework as social media.
bill:C-34:PassedHouseSecondReadingDateTi.short: C-34 (Safe Social Media Act) passes 2nd reading; would regulate AI chatbot services.

bill:C-297:PassedHouseFirstReadingDateTi.summary: New private member's bill C-297 would make it reviewable conduct under the Competition Act to set individual prices using automated decision-making and consumer data.
bill:C-297:PassedHouseFirstReadingDateTi.short: C-297 introduced: algorithmic personalized pricing would become reviewable under the Competition Act.

senate:103:46.summary: Government says Team Canada Strong will expand skilled trades training capacity through the Cadet and Junior Canadian Rangers programs.

senate:101:39.summary: A senator asks for Canada's position before treaty talks in Geneva on banning AI weapons.

senate:100:27.summary: In the Senate, the ESDC minister describes a new innovation stream in the Union Training and Innovation Program: funding for AI in construction techniques, more youth, women and Indigenous people in the trades, and training facilities.
senate:100:27.short: New UTIP innovation stream funds AI in construction and broader trades participation.

senate:100:52.summary: Senate agrees to extend the deadline for the Social Affairs committee's final report on the impact of artificial intelligence.

senate:96:41.summary: The Cutting Red Tape bill would let the Minister of Industry use automated decision-making to speed licensing of low-risk wireless devices.

senate:90:30.summary: Government says IRCC does not use AI to decide temporary foreign worker applications.

senate:90:32.summary: Government says it is expanding the AI Compute Access Fund by $700 million to help start-ups and smaller firms afford computing power.
senate:90:32.short: AI Compute Access Fund expanded by $700M.

senate:90:53.summary: Senate debate on the Building Canada Strong bill describes Team Canada Strong as an $8B federal–provincial investment in skilled trades training and Red Seal apprenticeship completion.

senate:89:41.summary: A senator asks why Canada did not support a UN resolution on human control over AI in nuclear command and control.

sen-notice:710268.summary: Senate Social Affairs AI study continues, with the Machine Intelligence Research Institute's CEO and Avi Goldfarb (Rotman) among witnesses.

sen-notice:709480.summary: Senate Transport and Communications committee is drafting its report on the opportunities and challenges of AI in the ICT sector.
sen-notice:709480.short: Senate Transport committee drafting report on AI in the ICT sector.

sen-cttee:/en/content/sen/committee/451/.summary: Witnesses tell the Senate Official Languages committee that AI was trained on writers' uncompensated work and is undermining their income.
A witness at Senate Foreign Affairs notes that Cohere is merging with a German company to build a larger AI firm.
Senate Social Affairs AI study hears from Nicolas Papernot, co-director of the Canadian AI Safety Institute research program at CIFAR, and other experts.
Senate Social Affairs AI study hears from CIGI's Global AI Risks Initiative and others, including on bringing AI into government consultations with civil society.
Canada's Building Trades Unions tell the Senate special committee on the Building Canada Strong Act that UTIP funding is expanding training centres, but apprentices also need work on projects.

sen-notice:706881.summary: Senate Human Rights committee is drafting its report on AI's impact on human rights and economic security, including vulnerable groups and the right to work.
sen-notice:706881.short: Senate Human Rights committee drafting report on AI, human rights and the right to work.

sen-cttee:/en/content/sen/committee/451/.summary: AI Minister Evan Solomon appears before the Senate Social Affairs committee's AI study. An ISED official says the 100,000 Red Seal placements complement the 90,000 placements in the AI for All strategy.
sen-cttee:/en/content/sen/committee/451/.short: AI Minister at Senate AI study; officials pair 100,000 Red Seal placements with 90,000 AI for All placements.

sen-notice:710396.summary: Upcoming at the Senate Social Affairs AI study: the Canadian Labour Congress, Ajay Agrawal and Wendy Cukier, on AI and work.

sen-notice:710604.summary: Upcoming at the Senate Social Affairs AI study: Valerio De Stefano (Osgoode) and Karen Hughes (University of Alberta).
